title: Make in batches and price each piece so it pays you

say: Make in batches, and price each piece so it pays you.
This is the video for module two of Handmade Accessories for Sale.
In this module you sew a lined tote, and make bracelets, earrings and headbands. The secret to doing it well is batching.

say: Making one pair of earrings from start to finish, then the next, means picking up the same tools again and again. Pieces come out different.

say: Batching means doing one step for all pieces before you move on. Glue dries while you work, and every piece matches.

say: For example, Ada in Enugu used to take about 25 minutes a pair. On a Saturday she tries a batch of ten pairs. First she cuts all 20 circles, choosing matching motifs in pairs.

panel.heading: Ada's batch of ten pairs
items: Assemble on ear wires: about 30 minutes

say: Then she presses all 20 buttons with her kit.

panel.heading: Ada's batch of ten pairs
items: Assemble on ear wires: about 30 minutes

say: Next she opens 20 jump rings. Twist the ends sideways, one towards you and one away. Never pull a ring open into an oval. That weakens the metal.

panel.heading: Ada's batch of ten pairs
items: Assemble on ear wires: about 30 minutes

say: Then she attaches the buttons to the ear wires.

panel.heading: Ada's batch of ten pairs
items: Assemble on ear wires: about 30 minutes

say: Last, she checks every pair and puts it on a card. Ten pairs took about 115 minutes, roughly 12 minutes a pair instead of 25.

panel.heading: Ada's batch of ten pairs
items: Assemble on ear wires: about 30 minutes
panel.rule: About 12 minutes a pair instead of 25.

say: A price has four parts. Materials are everything in one piece, including packaging and labels. Divide bulk prices by how many pieces they make.

panel.heading: What a price is built from
items: Labour: your time, at a fair hourly rate
Profit: money to restock and grow

say: Labour. Your time is a cost. Multiply a fair hourly rate by the time per piece from your batch timings.

panel.heading: What a price is built from
items: Labour: your time, at a fair hourly rate
Profit: money to restock and grow

say: Overhead is the cost of running the business: fuel or electricity, needles, data and transport. Add up a month, and divide by the pieces made.

panel.heading: What a price is built from
items: Labour: your time, at a fair hourly rate
Profit: money to restock and grow

say: Profit is money for the business itself, to buy stock, replace tools and grow.
Cost is materials plus labour plus overhead. Price is cost plus profit.

panel.heading: What a price is built from
items: Labour: your time, at a fair hourly rate
Profit: money to restock and grow

say: Let us cost a pair of Ada's earrings. These prices are approximate examples. Use your own receipts.
Two cover buttons, ear wires, jump rings, fabric, glue, a card and a small bag come to about 1,020 naira.
Her labour is 12 minutes a pair at 1,500 naira an hour. That is 300 naira.
Her overhead is about 6,000 naira a month across about 60 pieces. That is 100 naira a pair.
So one pair costs her 1,420 naira. Adding about 50 percent profit gives about 2,130.
She prices the pair at 2,500 naira, within the range of similar sellers.
A formula is the start, not the end. Compare your price with what your buyer already pays. If it is close, you are in range.

say: Keep every receipt. Your costing is only as accurate as your records.

panel.heading: Before you name a price
items: Build payment and POS fees into your price
Agree delivery costs in writing first

say: Payment links, POS charges and platform fees take a little from each sale. Check your provider's current fees, and build them into your price.

panel.heading: Before you name a price
items: Build payment and POS fees into your price
Agree delivery costs in writing first

say: Agree with the buyer in writing who pays for delivery before you send anything.

panel.heading: Before you name a price
items: Build payment and POS fees into your price

say: Material prices change often. Recheck them every time you restock, and at least every three months. And never sell below cost.

say: To remember. Batch one step across many pieces, and follow your recipe card. Open jump rings sideways.
Cost is materials plus labour plus overhead. Price is cost plus profit. And never sell below cost.
